en: The protector of the world-net, with a garland of skulls around his neck, with the autumn moon upon his forehead, the Death-deity to the great daityas,
possessing a body as blue as the sky, and whose illusory power is difficult to overcome.
I worship Him who has the beautiful lotus as His companion; I worship Him. 1.
Dwelling eternally in the ocean, with a smile of falling flowers, the abode of the world, possessing the radiance of a hundred suns,
bearing the mace and the discus as weapons, and clothed in shimmering yellow garments—
I worship, I worship Him whose face is beautiful with a smile. 2.
The necklace around the neck of Ramā, the essence of the multitude of Vedas,
sporting within the waters, the remover of the earth’s burden;
whose form is consciousness and bliss, and whose nature is most beautiful.
I worship Him who assumes many forms; I worship Him! 3.
Free from old age and birth, swollen with supreme bliss, absorbed in meditative concentration, and eternally undecaying;
the cause of the world's birth, the banner of the host of gods—
I worship Him, the sole bridge across the three worlds; I worship Him! || 4 ||
To him who has performed the chanting of the Vedas, whose vehicle is the lord of birds (Garuḍa), who is the cause of liberation, who humbles the pride of Śiva’s enemy (Kāma),
who is favorable to his devotees, and who is at the root of the tree of the universe.
I worship Him who has cast away all affliction and pain; I worship Him! I worship Him! 5.
The Lord of all the immortals, whose hair resembles black bees, who is but a minute fragment of the reflection of the universe, residing in the region of the space of the heart;
he whose body is eternally divine and from whom all worldly attachment has been forever released.
I worship the abode of Suvaikuṇṭha; I worship it! 6.
The most powerful among women, the most excellent in the three worlds,
the greatest among teachers, solely devoted to his own true nature,
ever courageous in battle, the hero of heroes.
I worship the shore of the great ocean; I worship it.
With Lakṣmī on his left side, with the serpent-king beneath his feet, having performed the required sacrifices, free from the passion of attachment,
praised by the lords of sages, and surrounded by the gods—
I worship Him who transcends the multitudes of qualities; I worship Him. 8.
The Declaration of the Fruit of the Teaching.
Whoever, constantly fixing their mind upon this, should recite this "Necklace of the Eight" of Murāri,
shall surely go to the sorrowless world of Viṣṇu.
One does not again experience old age, birth, and sorrow. || 9 ||
Thus ends the Śrīharistotra composed by the venerable Paramahaṃsa Svāmī Brahmananda.
